item.title: WPL 2027 schedule announced: Vadodara, Mumbai to host fifth edition; RCB face MI in opener
item.description: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Wednesday announced the schedule for the fifth edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL), with Vadodara and Mumbai set to host the tournament from January 14 to February 7, 2027. The 22-match competition will feature five franchises, with 11 matches scheduled at each venue. Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) will begin their title defence against former champions Mumbai Indians (MI) in the opening fixture at Vadodara on January 14. The fifth edition will begin with the Vadodara leg, which will run until January 24. The tournament will then move to Mumbai, with the Cricket Club of India's Brabourne Stadium hosting the remaining 11 matches from January 26. All matches, including the Playoffs, will begin at 7:30 PM IST. Brabourne Stadium to host Playoffs and final The league stage will continue in Mumbai until February 3, after which the tournament will enter the knockout phase. The Eliminator, featuring the teams finishing second and third in the league standings, will be played on February 5. The winner will advance to the final, where they will meet the table-toppers, who will earn direct qualification for the title clash. The final is scheduled for February 7 at the Brabourne Stadium, bringing the fifth edition of the WPL to a close. The five franchises will once again compete for the coveted title, with RCB entering the season as defending champions and looking to retain their crown. BCCI considering expansion of WPL The schedule announcement comes days after BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia indicated that the Board could explore expanding the league beyond its existing five-team structure. The WPL has featured five franchises since its inaugural edition in 2023, but the BCCI is now considering ways to increase participation and further develop the competition. "From next year, definitely we will have to do some brainstorming sessions to increase the number of teams as well as in other areas where we can improve," Saikia had said. "Not only the players but so many other areas we are having involvement in, right from the coaches, selectors, etc, and various stakeholders are involved here," he added. Saikia also highlighted the league's contribution to women's cricket in India, describing it as one of the biggest franchise competitions in the sport. "WPL is one of the big leagues in franchise cricket after IPL. We have come a long way in four years and ultimately we are now dominating women's cricket. WPL has contributed to the success of women's cricket in India," he said. Meanwhile, Sophie Molineux emerged as the costliest player at the recent auction, with UP Warriorz securing the services of the Australia captain for Rs 1.10 crore. The Brooklyn Nets should embrace their youth movement. At this point, the Nets are relying on a pair of veterans to do most of the heavy lifting. Bleacher Report's Zach Buckley argues that Brooklyn's "biggest problem" is that other Nets are getting the touches they need to become reliable offensive contributors. "Yet, their three minutes leaders are all in their age-27 seasons or older. Their offense runs first through 31-year-old Julius Randle and 28-year-old Michael Porter Jr.—two of the more logical trade candidates in the league. "The developmental minutes and touches that could go to the young players are too often winding up with (arguably) veteran placeholders," Buckley wrote. Porter is averaging 20.7 points per game, and Randle leads the team with 20.9 points per game. item.title: Sam Darnold injury: Seahawks QB out vs. Cardinals after injuring quad
item.description: (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The upcoming game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Seattle Seahawks has a bit more meaning thanks to results from Week 8. While the Cardinals pulled off a win in overtime against the Dallas Cowboys to improve to 3-5, the Seahawks dropped to 4-4 with a loss on Monday night to the Chicago Bears. That means that depending on how this game goes, as well as the Los Angeles Rams game against Washington Commanders, there is a world where the defending Super Bowl champions are in last place in the NFC West come Tuesday morning. And now, the Seahawks will be without their starting quarterback for the game. Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed on Wednesday that Sam Darnold suffered a quad injury during the loss to the Bears, and will be out for Week 8. Drew Lock will now start in his place. Lock is dealing with his own injury situation, as he was Seattle’s emergency third quarterback against Chicago last week. The backup quarterback is managing an elbow injury on his throwing arm, and was inactive for Seattle’s Week 7 game against the Kansas City Chiefs. When Darnold was injured earlier in the season, Lock stepped in and helped the Seahawks get out to a 2-0 start. He came in for an injured Darnold back in Week 1, completing 16-of-22 passes for 187 yards and a touchdown as Seattle came back to defeat the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl 60 rematch. He then started — against the Cardinals — and completed 19-of-26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns as Seattle beat Arizona 31-7.

item.title: Lee Westwood Remains Unemployed As LIV 2.0 Talks Stall
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Lee Westwood has entered a period of professional limbo, stating clearly that he has not signed a contract for the proposed LIV 2.0 tour. The 53-year-old Englishman, who joined the Saudi-backed league in 2022, described his current status as “unemployed” during a recent interview. This development comes as the league attempts to restructure its operations following significant financial turbulence. Westwood confirmed that he has not held any talks regarding a return to the DP World Tour, leaving his playing schedule wide open for the immediate future. The uncertainty surrounding the tour’s future has created a standoff between the organization and its veteran players. Sky Sports Golf reported that Westwood disclosed on The Chipping Forecast podcast that LIV 2.0 had not offered him “anything agreeable” regarding the league’s planned 2027 relaunch. The former world number one noted that while the new format is still being worked out, the terms offered so far do not meet his needs. BBC Sport reports that the league filed for bankruptcy protection last month after the Public Investment Fund withdrew its support, which had included an investment of more than $5 billion. Even so, BC Partners Credit could provide up to $300 million in financing to advance the project, giving the series that potential. The Cost of a Captaincy Decision Westwood’s career path was heavily influenced by a key choice made before the LIV era fully took hold. He was once a certain pick to captain Team Europe, a role that became a point of contention when the league arrived. Westwood explained that shortly after the 2021 Ryder Cup at Whistling Straits, he had a conversation with DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings about captaining the event in Italy. He asked Kinnings if he could still be Ryder Cup captain if he joined LIV. “They didn’t say no, but it was made clear that there would be very little chance of it, and I made the decision to go to LIV,” Westwood said in comments reported by Sky Sports Golf. Henrik Stenson’s choice differs from his own, as Stenson accepted the captaincy with the expectation of joining LIV, only to lose the position. Westwood reflected on the situation with a sense of finality. “But we make calls in life, you make a choice, and I have no regrets over the choice I made there,” he told Yahoo Sports . The Englishman tied Sir Nick Faldo for the most Ryder Cup appearances on 11 occasions during his last outing in 2021. While Luke Donald has since led Team Europe to success in Rome, Westwood’s path diverged. He noted that the captaincy “wasn’t the be-all and end-all for me” and admitted, “I’m not sure I wanted it enough.” This admission suggests that the prestige of the role did not outweigh the financial or structural appeal of the new league at that time. Weiss returned to the Braves as the bench coach in November 2017 and was with the team when they won the World Series. After Brian Snitker retired following the 2025 season, Weiss was named the manager. The Braves won the NL East in his first season, but were eliminated in the NLDS. The Braves have already made a front office change , hiring former Astros general manager Dana Brown as a senior adviser with amateur scouting. Now, the Braves and Weiss have made a decision on the coaching staff , according to Jesus Cano of The Athletic. “The Atlanta Braves will retain their entire coaching staff for the upcoming season, a team source familiar with the decision told The Athletic on the condition of anonymity to discuss personnel matters,” Cano wrote. item.title: NBA insider 'not closing the door' on Jalen Williams returning by 2027 NBA playoffs
item.description: On a random late October night, the Oklahoma City Thunder had both their season — and really, franchise — trajectory completely changed. Jalen Williams sustained a fractured fibula and a dislocated ankle in an Oct. 25 win over the LA Clippers . He's had surgery to fix both. Considering how gruesome the scene was, most assumed Williams would be out for the 2026-27 season. His leg snapped backward and needed to be stretchered off. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander covered his tears with his jersey. Chet Holmgren was in shock. Alex Caruso was mad at fate. But following his surgery, the Thunder left the door open. Williams will be re-evaluated before the 2026-27 regular season ends. Well, that's interesting. Of course, that doesn't mean he'll for sure come back like a Marvel superhero to help OKC make an improbable playoff run. But it leaves the thought in your mind for the next six months. Top NBA expert/insider Zach Lowe added fuel to the fire. He recently said on his The Ringer NBA podcast that Williams still has a slim chance to return before the 2027 NBA playoffs — as unfathomable as that sounds considering how traumatic the injury was for both himself and everybody who watched it. "I'm not closing the door on J-Dub returning in the playoffs. Assuming they make the playoffs. I'm expecting them to be out for the season, because we all saw what happened," Lowe said. "Based on what I've heard, I'm not closing the door until the Thunder actually publicly closed it." I guess we'll just see how things look in April. Both with Williams' lengthy recovery and where the Thunder are in the NBA standings. If they can hold down the fort as a top-four seed, you just never know. That said, I don't think OKC will recklessly rush him back for this upcoming postseason run. We just truly don't know. Only time will tell. But the Thunder purposely not ruling Williams out for the entire 2026-27 season — along with Cason Wallace as he had surgery to repair a torn labrum he sustained the same night — was a conscious decision to make. "I'm not closing the door on J-Dub returning in the playoffs… based on what I've heard, I'm not closing the door until the Thunder actually publicly close it." item.title: Bears Lose OT Braxton Jones for the Year
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Braxton Jones #70 of the Chicago Bears sits on the field after sustaining an injury during an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears received some unfortunate news on Wednesday, as offensive tackle Braxton Jones will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season. Jones underwent surgery on his right knee, officially ending any hopes of a return this season. Jones originally suffered the injury during Chicago’s Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, exiting the game in the third quarter. The Bears subsequently placed him on injured reserve on October 3, initially leaving the door open for a return after the mandatory four-game absence. Unfortunately, that return will no longer happen. From the Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs . Jones suffered a partially torn patellar tendon, and the plan was for him to rehabilitate the injury before determining if it was feasible for him to return this season and delay surgery. After a little more than a month, it was decided to have the injury repaired, an NFL source said Wednesday. The 27-year-old tackle entered the season having won the competition for the starting left tackle position after signing a one-year, 5 million dollar deal to remain in Chicago this past offseason. After starting the first three games, another injury has cut his season short, raising questions about his future with the organization. The 6-foot-5, 303-pound tackle is in his fifth NFL season, having spent his entire career in Chicago after being selected in the fifth round (168th overall) of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Southern Utah. Despite his relatively modest draft position, Jones has accumulated 47 starts in 49 career appearances, including starting all 17 games during his rookie campaign. For Jones, this is another frustrating setback in a career that has shown promise but has increasingly been interrupted by injuries. With his contract expiring after this season, it’s fair to wonder whether we’ve seen his final snap in a Bears uniform. Regardless of what happens next, here’s hoping Jones makes a full recovery. item.title: Saratoga Springs baseball standout Cody Mills commits to Lehigh
item.description: Saratoga batter Cody Mills makes contact makes contact during a game against Colonie on Tuesday, May 5, 2026, in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) Cody Mills embraced the challenge of being a young starter on a Saratoga Springs roster filled with seniors seeking a second straight Class AAA baseball state title in 2026. The Blue Streaks captured another sectional title and, while they did not win a state crown, Mills established himself as a force. As the standout third baseman continues to prepare for his second varsity baseball season, he does so with the knowledge of where his college destination will be, as Mills recently provided Lehigh coach Sean Leary his verbal commitment to compete for the Mountain Hawks of the Patriot League. Mills batted .362 as a sophomore. He launched three home runs and led the Blue Streaks with 35 RBIs, and earned Times Union second-team honors at third base. The Blue Streaks defeated Colonie in three games to claim the 2026 Class AAA sectional title before falling in the state tournament. "It was awesome and, by far, the most fun team I've ever been on," Mills said. "Playing with 14 or 15 seniors, I learned so much from them, and understanding the highs and lows. I had a great time. It was unfortunate the way that it ended. Overall, it was an amazing experience." "We were excited to have him on the squad last year and he contributed almost instantly," Saratoga Springs coach Andy Cuthbertson said. "He was consistent throughout and that was one of his highlights of the year, stepping in as a sophomore, contributing and doing so at a high level. He was one of the big reasons we were able to get that sectional championship." Mills, who plans to major in finance, selected Lehigh over several Ivy League programs. "It was great. Coach Cuthbertson put me in the lineup early and built up my confidence," Mills said. "It helped lead me to have a strong summer and fall." "The timing of him jumping on the squad last year and being around such a strong senior leadership group, with his brother (Brady, now at William & Mary) on the team, and you name the others, was just a good experience for him to see what it all looks like," Cuthbertson said. "He had such a positive year, defensively and offensively. Now, he will be coming into this season with a new level of confidence and he knows what a leader looks like. We're going to be turning to him." Cuthbertson believes Mills is poised to have a huge junior campaign for the Blue Streaks. Mills is looking forward to making another playoff push with a less-experienced squad in 2027. "A lot of the other Suburban Council teams have counted us out a little bit," Mills said. "We've got a bunch of new guys, but I think we are going to surprise some people. The past two years, we were the team to beat. This year, we will be more the hunter." (Photo by Michael Urakami/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The baseball postseason makes space for the unpredictable, but sometimes, it also brings to light what was clear all along. The Milwaukee Brewers won the World Series and deserved every bit of it. They were seen as the most likely squad to derail the Dodgers’ hopes of a threepeat, and ultimately they ran roughshod over the National League and beat the Rays to win it all. They did what they were expected to do based on a full season of excellence, and in fact, despite how MLB’s playoffs traffic in tiny samples, this postseason mostly served to highlight the obvious flaws in many would-be contenders, particularly in the American League, which only really produced a couple teams that impressed in 2026. First off, let’s start with an easy one regarding the Houston Astros, who in no way, shape, or form had a rotation that even remotely belonged in a playoff setting. Two games are just that, but the White Sox piling up 13 runs to sweep Houston in the AL Wild Card round felt justified given how poor Houston’s pitching was all year. In the series that followed, which pitted Chicago against Cleveland, there was no rhyme or reason to the AL Central race this season. It was a continuous cycle of mediocrity with no team capable of capitalizing on a weak field, and fittingly, the Guardians and White Sox delivered a back-and-forth series in the most bizarre way possible, with the road team winning the first four games before Cleveland completed comeback from down 2-0 with a win in Game 5. Now, we move on to the more important narratives in the AL East that were confirmed in the playoffs. Through 162 games, the Yankees survived Aaron Judge’s absence in large part thanks to Ben Rice’s glorious campaign and a dynamite pitching staff. Still, the offense was an issue for most the season, and it was let down by the likes of Trent Grisham and Jazz Chisholm Jr., who had in the past done enough for us to expect more from them but crashed and burned at the plate in 2026. item.title: Rory McIlroy voices support for DP World Tour, says LIV Golf 'turned professional golf into an arms race'
item.description: Rory McIlroy voiced his support for the DP World Tour Wednesday following comments made by CEO Guy Kinnings stating that LIV Golf aimed to "destroy" the Tour. Speaking to reporters in Abu Dhabi ahead of the Tour's penultimate tournament, the six-time major winner remained defiant when asked about LIV Golf's impact on professional tours and endorsed Kinnings's claims. "I agree with everything that Guy said. They took players, they took sponsors, they turned professional golf into an arms race," McIlroy said. "They were going around Augusta this year saying they wanted to destroy the European Tour." Kinnings has made it clear that players participating in LIV Golf 2.0 will be barred from playing on the DP World Tour in 2027, a firm shift after allowing LIV Golf eligibility since its inception in 2022. DP World Tour will no longer allow LIV Golf players to compete in 2027 Unlike the PGA Tour, which has barred members of LIV Golf from competition since its inception in 2022, the DP World Tour had granted eligibility to participate in tournaments. Mike Bachmann , "Myself and everyone at the DP World Tour have a duty to our members to protect our Tour," Kinnings said. "We are proud of that and are proud that we treat everyone who works for the tour, whether that be staff, suppliers, contractors, everyone, with respect and dignity." Players like Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia have elected to breakaway from LIV Golf. However, Kinnings reaffirmed that those who relinquished their DP World Tour membership will remain ineligible for Ryder Cup Captaincy. "The rule as it stands is that you have to have been in continuous membership to be considered for Captaincy," Kinnings said. This was introduced in 2017. Nobody even knew what LIV was then. Everyone believes it was done as a reaction to LIV but the truth is it wasn't." McIlroy revealed that he considered giving up his DP World Tour membership in 2019 to shift his focus primarily to the PGA Tour before Keith Pelley informed him that he'd relinquish any opportunity for Ryder Cup Captaincy. "I nearly made that choice and having that chat with Keith Pelley and knowing the rules, I was like 'Well, of course I want to be a Ryder Captain one day.' But everyone knows that rule, and everyone knows that if you abdicate your membership, that's the consequence." McIlroy believes there needs to be more "give and take" when it comes to sustainability and the overall health of the game, but affirms that "there has never been a better time to be a professional golfer." "Talk to Jack Nicklaus or any of these older guys, they would have loved LIV to come around in their day. They would have had more money, and we are all making more money because of it. But I do think there has to be a bit of a reset." The 37-year-old is pursuing his eighth Race to Dubai title that would tie him with Colin Montgomerie for the most in DP World Tour history.

I thought the offense would be the strength of this team. Here’s how it measured up against Washington: Points: 10 (target: 32) Yards per play: 5.2 Yards per pass attempt: 5.8 Explosive plays: 7 Third down: 7 of 13, the one situational target we hit Sacks allowed: 2 The red zone numbers are bad enough that all I can do is sigh. Nebraska culture has turned me into an Oscar-level sigher. Most of the explosive plays came in the first half, and somehow that turned into only seven points. In the second half they mostly dried up. Washington, meanwhile, got its big plays right at the end, when they counted most. 29 Runs, 44 Passes This is the stat that bothers me most. Jamal Rule ran 13 times for 72 yards, 5.5 yards a carry, with a long of 20. The run game was working. Nebraska ran 132 yards on the ground and threw for 255, but look at how the plays split: 29 carries and 44 pass attempts. I don’t understand that. I really don’t. Remember the Indiana game? item.title: Neemias Queta Stuns Celtics Fans By Starting Over Mitchell Robinson
item.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images Neemias Queta started at center for the Boston Celtics on Monday night, while Mitchell Robinson watched from the bench. The team signed Robinson to a three-year, $47 million deal on July 6. The former Knicks center is now the backup, and the numbers show why the change was necessary. Per Hardwood Houdini , the Celtics are a winning team when Robinson sits on the sideline, but they struggle badly when he plays. The data from the game against the Houston Rockets tells a clear story. In only 26 minutes of action, Queta recorded 16 points along with six rebounds. He made a corner three-pointer and grabbed four offensive boards. Robinson played 15 minutes and scored only four points. The 109-93 loss snapped Boston’s five-game win streak, dropping them to 5-2 on the season. Why the Bench Spot Hurts Robinson The season-long stats for the Celtics look terrible when Robinson is on the court. According to Hardwood Houdini, the team has a net rating of -35.1 when he plays. When he sits out, that number jumps to a league-best +16. His offensive rating while on the floor is 97.1, which would be the worst mark in the entire NBA. Without him, the offense shoots up to 123.5. These are not small differences. They show a massive gap in how the team performs with different players. Robinson also struggled to keep up with the pace of the game. He looked slow and out of shape against the physical Houston frontcourt. He was overmatched by Alperen Sengun and failed to create space with his screens. Queta, on the other hand, used his size to score Boston’s first seven points of the night. He even converted two offensive rebounds into tip-ins. The former Knicks star had no deflections or screen assists to his name, while Queta recorded four deflections and three screen assists. Coach Mazzulla Embraces the Change Joe Mazzulla made the starting lineup change to use the team’s depth and variety. “Just taking advantage of our depth, taking advantage of our variety,” Mazzulla said after the loss. He noted that he puts the same weight into every lineup he uses. The coach changed the lineup at halftime to put Queta back in the starting five. The visitors had already reduced their deficit to 68-62 when Robinson joined Queta in a twin-tower lineup to start the second half. The Celtics rolled with multiple double-big looks against Houston to handle the physical play. They started with Queta and Luka Garza, then added Robinson later. This look will likely appear again as the season goes on. The team is 5-2 despite the issues with Robinson, but the front office must decide if his current form is sustainable. The three-year deal is guaranteed, yet the best version of the player has not shown up yet.
